essence: Sophronia is two half-cities, a fairground of rides that stays and a city of stone, marble and cement that is dismantled every year and hauled away on trailers, leaving the carnival to count the days until life is whole again.
textDetails: Sophronia is made of two half-cities.
One half holds a great roller coaster with steep humps, a carousel whose spokes are chains, and a Ferris wheel of spinning cages.
Also in that half: a death-ride with crouching motorcyclists (in the Italian original a 'well of death' with riders head-down) and a circus big top with a cluster of trapezes hanging in the middle.
The other half is of stone, marble and cement, with the bank, the factories, the palaces, the slaughterhouse, the school and all the rest.
One half-city is permanent and the other temporary; when its stay is over, the temporary one is uprooted, dismantled and moved to the vacant lots of another half-city.
The temporary half is the stone one: every year workmen detach the marble pediments and lower the stone walls and the cement pylons.
They take down the Ministry, the monument, the docks, the petroleum refinery and the hospital.
Everything is loaded onto trailers that follow, from stand to stand, a yearly itinerary.
What stays behind is the half-Sophronia of shooting galleries and carousels.
A scream remains hanging in the air from the car of the roller coaster at its headlong plunge.
The remaining half begins counting the months and days until the caravan returns and complete life can start again.
Not in the text: season, time of day, lights, colours, the form of the vehicles beyond 'trailers'; the dusk, the bulbs and the plan are design choices.
visualConcept: A round plinth like a coin cut in two: a straight boulevard splits it down the middle and the two halves could not be more different, so the double nature reads at a glance. On the left lies the fairground, a permanent landscape of thin lattice steel, canvas and light: the great roller coaster circling the outer edge on spindly trestles with a chain of steep humps, a tall wheel whose cages spin as it turns, a chain carousel flinging its seats outward, the wooden drum of the well of death with tiny motorcyclists crouched on its inner wall, a striped big top whose translucent canvas reveals a cluster of trapezes hanging in the middle, and a row of shooting galleries, all strung with chasing bulbs. On the right stands the stone city, pale, dense and solemn: a pedimented bank, a colonnaded Ministry, palaces, a school, a hospital, factories with sawtooth roofs and cement chimneys, a slaughterhouse with pens, a monument on a square, a march of cement pylons, a petroleum refinery of tanks, columns and a flare, and docks with cranes along a crescent of dark harbour water at the plinth's far rim. Every stone building is subtly a kit, with visible seams between pediment, columns and wall panels, lifting eyes on the roofs and numbered blocks, as if made to be packed. From the stone half's outer edge a road leaves the plinth and runs on as a ramp into the fog, where a line of empty flatbed trailers waits with lamps lit. The irony that makes Sophronia unmistakable is staged by the light: the frivolous half blazes and moves, the serious half is grey and still, and it is the serious half that is about to leave.
layout: Plinth: disc of radius 23, thickness 1.5, top at y=0, split by a 2.5-wide boulevard along the north-south axis at x=0. Fairground (x<0): roller coaster on a closed spline hugging the west rim, about 60 units of track with 6 humps of height 1.5-4.5, lattice trestles every 0.8 units, a train of 3 cars; Ferris wheel of radius 3.2 with its hub at y=3.6 and 12 open cage gondolas, at (-6, 0, -9); chain carousel at (-11, 0, 3) with canopy radius 1 and 16 seats on chains 1.2 long; well of death at (-5, 0, 8), a wooden drum of radius 0.8 and height 0.8 with an outside stair and viewing rim, 2 riders; big top at (-14, 0, -2), radius 3, two king poles, peak 2.8, red-and-cream striped canvas at about 35 percent opacity with 8 trapezes clustered under the peak; 4 shooting-gallery booths with striped awnings along the boulevard; bulb strings on poles (several thousand emissive instanced points). Stone half (x>0): central square at (9, 0, 0) with the monument (column 3 tall with statue); Ministry (6 x 2.5 x 2.2, 12 columns, pediment) facing the square; bank (2.5 x 2 x 2, 4 columns, pediment); 2 palaces (3 x 3 x 2.4); school (U-plan 3 x 2.5 x 1.4 with a small bell turret); hospital (6 x 1.6 x 2, many windows); slaughterhouse (low sheds 4 x 2 x 0.8 with pens); 3 factories (sawtooth roofs, 3 x 2 x 1.2, cement chimneys 4 tall); refinery in the north-east (6 cylindrical tanks of radius 0.6-1, 2 distillation columns 5 tall, pipe racks, flare stack 7 tall); docks along the east rim, a crescent of water 3 wide inside the rim with stone quays and 2 harbour cranes 3.5 tall; a line of 6 cement pylons 2.5 tall carrying cables from the refinery toward the centre; about 120 generic stone blocks (1 x 1 x 0.8-2) filling the streets. Road: from the east rim a 2-wide road leaves the plinth as a straight ramp into the fog, with 14 flatbed trailers and tractor cabs parked along it. People: about 150 figures 0.25 tall, crowded in the fairground, fewer and more orderly in the stone streets.
signatureMotion: 1) The fair never stops: the wheel turns once in about 40 s while each cage spins on its own pivot, the chain carousel whirls with its seats flaring out to about 40 degrees, the coaster train crawls up each hump and plunges with gravity-like acceleration (lap about 18 s), motorcyclists race round the inner wall of the well of death, trapezes swing under the big top, and bulb chases ripple along the strings. 2) The stone half moves soberly: smoke from factory chimneys and the slaughterhouse, the refinery flare flickering, dock cranes inching, lit windows switching on one by one. 3) The yearly departure and return of the stone city, driven by the toggle (optionally also on a slow automatic cycle every few minutes).
interactionDescription: Plays the annual departure over about 12 s: marble pediments lift off on crane hooks, stone walls fold down into stacked flat panels, cement pylons tip and lie flat, and the Ministry, monument, docks, refinery and hospital collapse into neat crates that slide onto the flatbed trailers; the convoy then drives off along the ramp and dissolves into the fog. The east half is left as vacant lots with chalk outlines of footprints. The fairground keeps glowing, but the coaster train halts at the lip of its steepest drop with a small frozen ring of light hanging above it, the scream held in the air, and a tally of days begins lighting bulb by bulb on the fairground's gate sign. Toggling again brings the caravan back out of the fog: the city unfolds, rises and locks into place, the coaster is released into its plunge, and the whole city lives again.
mood: Late summer dusk at the blue hour: a deep indigo sky with a rose afterglow along the horizon; the fairground blazes with warm bulbs, red-and-cream canvas and a few mint highlights, haloed by bloom; the marble half is cool, pale and still, lit by sparse white street lamps and a few windows; low violet fog pools around the plinth and swallows the road. Festive and melancholy at once, the feeling of a fair at the end of the season.
caption: In Sophronia it is not the carnival that travels. The roller coaster, the wheel of spinning cages and the riders circling the well of death stay where they are. What leaves, every year, is the bank, the ministry, the hospital and the refinery, their marble pediments lifted off and stacked onto trailers. The rides wait in the half-empty dark, a cry hanging above the coaster's drop, counting days until the city is whole.
motto: Here the carnival is permanent; it is seriousness that goes on tour.
camera: Elevated three-quarter view from the south, looking north along the boulevard so the fairground fills the left half of the frame and the stone city the right: camera about 52 units from the centre, elevation about 30 degrees, target (1, 1.5, 0), FOV about 35. During the departure the camera drifts east to follow the convoy toward the fog, then settles back.
